title: Toward Effective and Reliable LLM Agents via Dynamic Ontology
thesis: Ontology can act as a kernel for agents: task-oriented ontologies and knowledge graphs are constructed dynamically and refined using judge feedback (OaK).
mechanism: Dynamic construction of task-oriented ontology/KG, iterative refinement driven by judge feedback.
evidence: Datasets, baselines, metrics and quantitative results not recovered in this session.
limitations: Unverified: evaluation scope, cost of judge loop, drift of refined ontology. Full text not read.
implications: Closest external analogue to World0 dynamic concept/relation evolution. Judge-feedback refinement could drive relation retyping and card merging. Risk: task-oriented ontologies may be too narrow versus World0's context-sensitive projection of one shared structure.

title: Remember Before You're Asked: MemDream for Self-Probing Memory Evolution
thesis: Memory should be repaired offline before retrieval fails, via self-probing dream cycles.
mechanism: Offline dream cycles with three agents (Dreamer, Analyst, Consolidator) that probe, diagnose and repair a memory graph; policy trained with GRPO; soft decay gives reversible forgetting; online interaction continues during consolidation.
evidence: Numerical results not recovered in this session.
limitations: Unverified: benchmark coverage, RL training cost, whether repairs introduce semantic drift.
implications: Maps directly onto a World0 Dream Mechanism: probe the concept-world with synthetic task contexts, diagnose weak projections, repair relations. Reversible decay matches the 'never silently delete' stance. Complexity: medium-high; start with a non-RL probe/diagnose/repair loop using the existing projection eval scripts.

title: Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation for Long-Term LLM Agents (REALM)
thesis: Organize memories into a heterogeneous cognitive graph and revise them from retrieval feedback.
mechanism: Heterogeneous cognitive graph; reconsolidation triggered by retrieval outcomes.
implications: Retrieval/projection feedback as a signal for relation weight updates.

assessment.observations: World0 probe E-004 (bigworld seed 0): of 101 pruned gold endpoints that focus queries missed, 65 had never appeared in any view; rehearsal on read could save at most about one in ten.
assessment.interpretation: Rewriting memories when they are read conflicts with World0's pure projection (reads do not change state, Corollary 3.2'). The borrowable form, rehearsal (reads refresh recency), was tested and refuted (H-004).
assessment.speculation: Retrieval feedback might still be usable as an explicit, separate observation event rather than a side effect of reading (see H-003).

title: Governing Evolving Memory in LLM Agents: Risks, Mechanisms, and the Stability and Safety Governed Memory (SSGM) Framework
thesis: Evolving agent memory needs governance; consolidation should be a write-validation step guarding against logical drift.
mechanism: Governed memory framework with validation on consolidation writes.
implications: Validation gate for concept-card and relation writes by LLMs (concept integrity, priority 1 in AGENTS.md).

title: SCM: Sleep-Consolidated Memory with Algorithmic Forgetting for Large Language Models
thesis: Combine working-memory limits, NREM/REM-style phases, intentional forgetting and a computational self-model for introspection.
mechanism: Sleep-phase consolidation plus adaptive forgetting plus self-model.
evidence: Search summary reports perfect recall over ten-turn conversations and 90.9% memory-noise reduction on an eight-test suite (prototype scale; not independently checked).
limitations: Small-scale prototype per summary; not read.
implications: Only found paper pairing a self-model with offline consolidation; evidence weak.

title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
thesis: Parametric consolidation: Knowledge Seeding then a RL-driven 'Dreaming' phase generating synthetic rehearsal curricula.
limitations: Parametric, outside World0 scope (conceptual structure, not weights).
implications: Low direct relevance; useful as contrast.

title: TRUSTMEM: Learning Trustworthy Memory Consolidation for LLM Agents with Long-Term Memory
thesis: Trustworthy consolidation (title only).
implications: Triage later.

assessment.interpretation: Learned consolidation and trust scoring is the opposite route to World0, whose belief and evidence are explicit counts of confirmations, withdrawals and denials.

title: Selective Forgetting: A Graph-Based Memory Framework for Long-Term LLM Agents
thesis: A graph memory can be pruned by recency, frequency and structural importance with little loss of retrieval quality.
mechanism: Each memory node gets a forgetting score combining recency, access frequency and structural (graph) importance; low-scoring nodes are pruned.
evidence: The authors claim retrieval quality stays nearly unchanged after pruning (search summary; numbers not recovered).
limitations: Not read: benchmarks, pruning rates and failure cases unknown.
implications: Same design as World0: decay depends on maturity and evidence, and the CORE gate counts surviving connections (structural importance). No new rule to borrow.

title: LycheeMemory V2 … Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation (title abbreviated in the search result)
thesis: Consolidate stored memory at the level of semantic segments.
implications: A memory-layer technique for stored text; outside World0's conceptual boundary.

title: Control-Plane Placement Shapes Forgetting: … Thirteen System Configurations (title abbreviated in the search result)
thesis: Where the control plane sits in an agent memory system determines how it forgets (from the title).
implications: Triage later; could inform where World0's decay sits relative to the agent loop.

title: FSFM: A Biologically-Inspired Framework for Selective Forgetting of Agent Memory
thesis: Agent forgetting serves three purposes, efficiency, quality and safety, and should be designed per purpose.
implications: Quality forgetting (updating stale preferences) corresponds to World0's withdrawal and denial; safety forgetting (active deletion) is absent from World0 and should stay out of the core.

title: From Recall to Forgetting: Benchmarking Long-Term Memory for Personalized Agents
thesis: Long-term memory benchmarks must test correctly forgetting outdated information, not only recall.
implications: Borrowable: LongRun's stale queries cover only explicit revisions. The roadmap-0.4 'silently outdated information' scenario can follow this benchmark's protocol.

title: HeLa-Mem: Hebbian Learning and Associative Memory for LLM Agents
thesis: Hebbian co-activation and associative recall give agents efficient long-term memory (ACL 2026).
mechanism: Co-activated memories strengthen their links; a reflective agent condenses dense hubs into semantic summaries.
evidence: Search summary: leads on four LoCoMo categories with fewer tokens (not independently checked).
limitations: Not read. Condensing hubs into summaries trades explicit structure for text.
implications: Same primitives as World0 (Hebbian co-occurrence learning with a Jaccard gate). Hub condensation resembles World0's reflect communities, which projection does not yet use; a candidate, deferred because it leans toward summary storage.

assessment.interpretation: Independent convergence on World0's activation primitives; no change warranted.

title: SYNAPSE: Episodic-Semantic Memory via Spreading Activation
thesis: Spreading activation over an episodic-semantic graph improves multi-hop recall (Findings of ACL 2026).
mechanism: Energy spreads along temporal and causal edges with lateral inhibition and temporal decay.
evidence: Search summary: leads LoCoMo multi-hop (not independently checked).
implications: Same as World0 (spreading activation with decay). Lateral inhibition is handled in World0 by projection-level MMR redundancy, not in the activation layer.

title: RoMem (full title not recorded)
thesis: Superseded facts should be suppressed, not deleted.
mechanism: Superseded facts are phase-rotated in a complex vector space so that retrieval ranking pushes stale facts down.
implications: Same goal, different mechanism: World0 uses explicit withdrawal, support outvoting and denial on typed claims.

title: TOKI: A Bitemporal Operator Algebra for Contradiction Resolution in LLM-Agent Persistent Memory
thesis: Contradictions in persistent agent memory are resolved at write time using both valid time and system time.
limitations: Identifier and full text not found.
implications: World0 records only system time (discovered_tick / retracted_tick), not valid time; an append-only event log is a roadmap-0.4 item. Prompted exposing claim system time in the API (Claim.since_tick / until_tick).

title: [Title not recovered] Deterministic version-aware aggregation for memory conflicts on MemoryAgentBench
thesis: Deterministic, version-aware aggregation resolves memory conflicts better than asking an LLM to resolve them.
evidence: Search summary: beats LLM conflict resolution on MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation (numbers not recovered).
implications: Supports World0's deterministic claim identity plus withdrawal over LLM arbitration.

title: Global Workspace Agents ("Theater of Mind")
thesis: A global-workspace cognitive loop improves agent reasoning.
mechanism: Generate several candidate thoughts, critique them, meta-select one; short-term memory over a threshold is compressed and archived.
implications: World0's focus (formal model §8) is the minimal form of the same theory; World0 does not generate thoughts, which is outside its boundary.

title: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents (survey)
thesis: Survey / evaluation reference; uses the LoCoMo and LongMemEval protocols.
implications: LoCoMo and LongMemEval are the field's main evaluations. LongRun's synthetic worlds are orthogonal (the generator defines the gold, every system reads the same extractions); connecting World0 to LoCoMo is a medium-term option that needs real extraction and a real reader.
